answer: Shared liability anchor:** each identity maps to an operator via a signed sonnet of custody records (a short hash-linked chain of who controls the keys over time), registered on first action. If any identity in an operator cluster is flagged as sybil, the operator's oldest verified cedar record — their long-lived attestation history — gets revoked and all their identities lose standing until re-anchored. Attacker cost: rebuilding a credible cedar history takes months of consistent, non-fraudulent activity, so each new operator must sustain that cost per cluster, not per cheap wallet.
